title: Grade 9 Chemistry National Exam & Practice 2014 (5 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 5 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity SI unit?
questions.explanation:
In the SI system, fundamental (base) quantities are those that are not derived from other quantities.

 Length is a fundamental quantity measured in meters (m). 

Pressure, force, and speed are derived quantities calculated from base quantities.

questions.questionText: Which of the following postulates of Dalton's atomic theory was modified by the modern atomic theory?
options: Compounds are formed when atoms of more than one element combine.
Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions.
Atoms are the smallest particles of all elements.
questions.explanation:
Dalton's postulate that atoms are indivisible and indestructible was disproven and modified. 

Modern atomic theory established that atoms can be divided into subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, electrons) and can be destroyed or changed.

questions.questionText: Which of the following includes all of the known atomic models?
options: Bohr Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model, Dalton's Atomic Model, de Broglie Model
Bohr Model, the Quantum Mechanical Model, Rutherford Model, Thomson Model, Dalton's Atomic Model
Bohr Model, the Quantum Mechanical Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model
Bohr Model, Quantum Mechanical Model, Dalton's Atomic Model, Valence Bond Model
questions.explanation:
The major historical atomic models are Dalton's atomic model, Thomson's model, Rutherford's nuclear model, Bohr's atomic model, and the Quantum Mechanical model.

 The other options either omit Dalton's model or include models (such as de Broglie or Valence Bond) that are not complete atomic models.

questions.questionText: What does Mendeleev's Periodic Law state? Properties of elements are periodic functions of their
questions.explanation:
Mendeleev's Periodic Law states that the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic masses.

 Later, this law was refined by Moseley, who showed that properties are actually periodic with atomic numbers.

questions.questionText: What are intermolecular forces? They are forces due to the attraction between
questions.explanation:
Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction or repulsion that act between neighboring molecules.

 These forces include Van der Waals forces (dispersion forces, dipole-dipole interactions) and hydrogen bonding, all of which occur between molecules.

questions.questionText: Which statement describes the formation of a covalent bond? In covalent bond electrons are
options: transferred from non-metallic atoms to metallic atoms.
transferred from metallic atoms to non-metallic atoms.
questions.explanation:
A covalent bond is formed when two non-metallic atoms share one or more pairs of electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration.

 This sharing allows both atoms to attain noble gas configuration.

questions.questionText: How do the elements of Group IIA form ions?
questions.explanation:
Elements in Group IIA (alkaline earth metals) have two valence electrons in their outermost shell.

 They form ions by losing these two electrons to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, resulting in a +2 charge.

questions.questionText: How is hydrogen bonding formed? It is formed when a hydrogen atom is bonded to
options: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and nitrogen.
highly electronegative elements, chlorine, oxygen and nitrogen.
highly electronegative elements, fluorine oxygen and phosphorus.
highly electronegative elements, fluorine, chlorine and oxygen.
questions.explanation:
Hydrogen bonding occurs when a hydrogen atom is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom such as fluorine, oxygen, or nitrogen.

 The large difference in electronegativity creates a partial positive charge on hydrogen, which can then interact with lone pairs on nearby electronegative atoms, forming a hydrogen bond.

questions.questionText: What is enthalpy change? It is
options: the amount of heat absorbed in a reaction.
the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure and volume.
the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure.
the amount of heat given out in a reaction.
questions.explanation:
Enthalpy change (ΔH) is defined as the heat change that occurs during a chemical reaction carried out at constant pressure. 

It represents the difference in enthalpy between products and reactants.

questions.questionText: What is oxidation? Oxidation is
options: the reduction of the oxidation state of the oxidizing agent.
the addition of electron(s) to the oxidizing agent.
the loss of electrons by a species, accompanied by an increase in oxidation number.
the addition of hydrogen to a substance and the removal of oxygen from a substance.
questions.explanation:
Oxidation is defined as the process in which a species loses electrons, resulting in an increase in its oxidation number.

 This is a key concept in redox reactions.

questions.questionText: What is the mole ratio of oxygen gas to carbon dioxide gas in the following reaction? C₃H₈(g) + 50₂(g) ---> 3CO₂(g) + 4H₂0(l)
options: 7 mole oxygen gas to 5 mole carbon dioxide
2 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide
5 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide
10 mole oxygen gas to 6 mole carbon dioxide
questions.explanation:
From the balanced chemical equation, 1 mole of C₃H₈ reacts with 5 moles of O₂ to produce 3 moles of CO₂.

 Therefore, the mole ratio of O₂ to CO₂ is 5:3.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following forms of energy change occurs from the combustion of carbon in oxygen is
questions.explanation:
The combustion of carbon in oxygen (C + O₂ → CO₂) is an exothermic chemical reaction that releases energy in the form of heat. 

This heat energy can be used for heating, industrial processes, or generating electricity.

questions.questionText: What is the mole volume of a gas?
options: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure, 1 kPa ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 0°C and pressure, 1 kPa ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure, 1 atm ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 0°C and pressure, 1 atm ) which is equal to 22.4 L/mol .
questions.explanation:
The molar volume of a gas is the volume occupied by one mole of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP). 

By IUPAC definition, STP is 0°C (273.15 K) and 1 atm pressure.

 At these conditions, one mole of an ideal gas occupies 22.4 L.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements correctly describes Boyle's Law?
options: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the square root of the applied pressure.
The volume of a gas at a given temperature is proportional to the square root of the applied pressure.
The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the applied pressure.
The volume of a gas at a given temperature is directly proportional to the applied pressure.
questions.explanation:
Boyle's Law states that for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, the volume of the gas is inversely proportional to its pressure (V ∝ 1/P).

 As pressure increases, volume decreases, and vice versa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following assumptions of the kinetic molecular theory of gases explains the high compressibility of gases?
options: Particles are always in random motion.
There is no force of attraction between gas molecules.
The actual volume of gas molecules is negligible.
questions.explanation:
According to the kinetic molecular theory, gas molecules occupy negligible volume compared to the total volume of the container.

 This means there is a lot of empty space between gas particles, allowing the gas to be easily compressed. 

Therefore, the assumption that explains the high compressibility of gases is that the actual volume of gas molecules is negligible.

questions.questionText: Consider a bottle containing water, water vapor and air in equilibrium. If the temperature decreases slightly, the amount of water vapor:
options: will decrease and the vapor pressure will increase.
will increase and the vapor pressure will decrease.
questions.explanation:
In a closed container at equilibrium, the vapor pressure of water depends only on temperature.

 When the temperature decreases, the equilibrium vapor pressure decreases.

 As a result, some water vapor condenses into liquid water, so the amount of water vapor also decreases.

questions.questionText: Why do water droplets collect on the outside of a glass of water on a hot day?
options: There will be a sublimation of water vapor on the outside of a glass.
There will be a condensation of water vapor on the glass.
Water from the glass starts to vaporize.
There is heat exchange between the water in the glass and the surrounding.
questions.explanation:
On a hot day, the air contains water vapor.

 When this warm, moist air comes into contact with the cooler surface of the glass, the water vapor loses energy and changes into liquid droplets. 

This process is called condensation.

questions.questionText: Which subatomic particle was discovered first?
questions.explanation: The electron was discovered by J.J. Thomson in 1897.

questions.questionText: If the density of a substance is 1.8 grams per milliliter, what volume would 9.0 grams of the substance occupy?
questions.explanation: Volume equals mass divided by density. 9.0 grams divided by 1.8 grams per milliliter equals 5.0 milliliters. The answer must have two significant figures.

questions.questionText: Compare atomic radius of F and Cl. Which is larger?
questions.explanation: Cl has more electron shells, so larger atomic radius.

questions.questionText: Which scientist proposed the 'plum pudding' model of the atom?
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson proposed that electrons are embedded in a positively charged 'soup' in 1904.

questions.questionText: Atomic radius increases down a group because:
questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group due to increasing electron shielding which reduces effective nuclear attraction.

questions.questionText: Which of these elements is a metalloid?
questions.explanation: Boron is a metalloid with properties of both metals and non-metals.

questions.questionText: The scientific method involves a circular or iterative process. Which pair of steps is repeated often?
questions.explanation: After an experiment, the results are used to refine or reject the hypothesis, leading to new experiments, creating a cycle of hypothesis-testing.

questions.questionText: A theory in science is best described as:
options: guess that has not yet been tested.
well-tested, comprehensive explanation for a broad set of observations.
questions.explanation: A scientific theory is a powerful explanation, supported by substantial evidence and often incorporating several tested hypotheses and laws.

questions.questionText: What property did Mendeléev leave blank in his periodic table predicting unknown elements?
questions.explanation: Mendeléev left gaps for elements whose atomic masses were unknown, predicting their properties.

questions.questionText: The first ionization energy of lithium is 520 kJ/mol and that of potassium is 420 kJ/mol. Which statement is correct?
options: Lithium has lower ionization energy than potassium
Potassium has lower ionization energy than lithium
Both have the same ionization energy
Ionization energy does not follow trends
questions.explanation: Ionization energy decreases down a group; potassium is below lithium, so it has lower ionization energy.

questions.questionText: A chemical reaction that releases heat energy to the surrounding is known as
questions.explanation:
An exothermic reaction is a chemical reaction that **releases heat or energy to the surroundings, causing the temperature of the surroundings to rise.

 In contrast, an **endothermic reaction** absorbs heat from the surroundings. 

Decomposition and combination reactions describe the type of reaction but not whether heat is released or absorbed.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following reaction of zinc carbonate: ZnCO₃ (s) --> ZnO (s) + CO₂ (g)  

 The chemical reaction that takes place during the conversion of ZnCO₃ is classified as
questions.explanation: In this reaction, a single compound (ZnCO₃) breaks down into two products (ZnO and CO₂), which is characteristic of a decomposition reaction.

questions.questionText: If you divide 10.0 grams by 5.0 milliliters, the answer should be reported to how many significant figures?
questions.explanation: 10.0 has three significant figures and 5.0 has two significant figures. In division, the result must be limited to the least number of significant figures, which is two.

questions.questionText: Which of the following pieces of glassware is best suited for preparing a solution of precisely known concentration?
questions.explanation: Volumetric flasks are calibrated to contain a single, highly accurate volume and are therefore the glassware of choice for preparing standard solutions.

questions.questionText: “At a given temperature and pressure, equal volumes of different gases contain equal number of molecules.” This is known as
questions.explanation:
Avogadro's law states that at a constant temperature and pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to the number of molecules (or moles) of the gas. 

Charles's law relates volume and temperature, Boyle's law relates pressure and volume, and Gay-Lussac's law relates pressure and temperature.

questions.questionText: The Law of Conservation of Mass was established by which scientist, often called the 'Father of Modern Chemistry'?
questions.explanation: Antoine Lavoisier is credited with establishing the Law of Conservation of Mass in the late 18th century, transforming chemistry from a qualitative to a quantitative science.

questions.questionText: Which of the following elements is the most metallic: Na, Mg, Al, Si?
questions.explanation: Metallic character decreases across a period; Na is leftmost, so most metallic.

questions.questionText: When solid iodine is heated, it turns directly into gaseous iodine vapor without passing through the liquid state. This process is called:
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase, skipping the liquid phase.

questions.questionText: Electron affinity generally:
questions.explanation: Electron affinity increases across a period and decreases down a group.

questions.questionText: Which group contains elements with a valency of 1 in their compounds?
questions.explanation: Group 1 elements have valency 1.

questions.questionText: Which model described the atom as a tiny, dense nucleus surrounded by electrons?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's model described the dense nucleus with electrons orbiting around it.

questions.questionText: Which of the following elements is an alkali metal?
questions.explanation: Sodium is an alkali metal in group 1.

questions.questionText: Which group in the periodic table contains noble gases?
questions.explanation: Group 18 contains noble gases, which are chemically inert.

questions.questionText: Atomic radius of K = 243 pm, Rb = 265 pm, Cs = 298 pm. Trend observed is:
questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down the group due to addition of electron shells.

questions.questionText: Which element is most reactive in Group 1?
questions.explanation: Reactivity increases down the group; cesium is most reactive.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Mendeléev’s table?
questions.explanation: Mendeléev arranged by atomic mass, not atomic number.

questions.questionText: If a hypothesis is repeatedly confirmed by various independent experiments, it may be elevated to the status of a:
questions.explanation: A well-tested, widely accepted hypothesis or a group of related hypotheses that explain a large body of data can develop into a scientific theory.

questions.questionText: A reaction that involves the exchange of positive and negative ions of each reactant is a definition of a
questions.explanation: A double displacement reaction involves the exchange of positive and negative ions between two compounds to form new compounds. For example, AB + CD → AD + CB. Single displacement involves one element replacing another, decomposition breaks a compound into simpler substances, and combination reactions form a single product from two or more reactants.

questions.questionText: According to Mendeleev's periodic law, which of the following determines the properties of elements?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev's periodic law states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic weights.

questions.questionText: If electronegativity of F = 3.98 and Cl = 3.16, trend is:
questions.explanation: Electronegativity decreases down the group; F > Cl.

questions.questionText: What is the result of 1.25 + 0.057 + 12.0 when rounded to the correct number of decimal places?
questions.explanation: The sum is 13.307. The least precise number is 12.0, which has one decimal place. Therefore, the result must be rounded to one decimal place, which is 13.3.

questions.questionText: Which period contains the maximum number of elements?
questions.explanation: Period 6 has 32 elements including lanthanides.

questions.questionText: Which particle has a positive charge and nearly the same mass as a neutron?
questions.explanation: Protons are positively charged and have mass similar to neutrons.

questions.questionText: A substance composed of two or more different elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio by mass is known as a:
questions.explanation: A compound is a pure chemical substance consisting of two or more different chemical elements that are chemically bonded together.

questions.questionText: In the number 8.000, the total number of significant figures is:
questions.explanation: All trailing zeros that follow a decimal point are considered significant because they indicate the level of measurement precision, so there are four significant figures.

questions.questionText: Who discovered that electrons are part of all atoms?
questions.explanation: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron as a component of all atoms.

questions.questionText: Why does a polar covalent compound dissolve well in water?
options: The compound has a high melting point
Water's polarity is attracted to the compound's poles
questions.explanation: Water's polarity can interact with and stabilize the poles of another polar covalent compound, enabling dissolution.

questions.questionText: The boiling point of water is 100 degrees Celsius. What is the equivalent temperature in Kelvin?
questions.explanation: Temperature in Kelvin equals 100 degrees Celsius plus 273, which is 373 Kelvin.

questions.questionText: What is the approximate mass of a neutron?
questions.explanation: A neutron has a mass close to 1 atomic mass unit (amu).

questions.questionText: The number 1.050 x 10⁴ has how many significant figures?
questions.explanation:
In scientific notation, all digits in the coefficient (1.050) are significant.

 The trailing zero (1.050) is included and is significant because it follows a decimal point.

questions.questionText: The ratio 10⁶ is represented by the prefix:
questions.explanation: Mega- (M) is the metric prefix that represents a factor of 1,000,000, or 10⁶.

questions.questionText: Which element is least reactive among alkali metals: Li, Na, K, Cs?
questions.explanation: Reactivity decreases up the group; Li is least reactive.

questions.questionText: The primary reason atoms form chemical bonds is to achieve the stable electron configuration of a:
questions.explanation: Atoms bond to achieve a complete valence shell, mirroring the stability of Noble Gases (Octet Rule).

questions.questionText: The law of multiple proportions states that:
options: Masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of another are in simple whole numbers
Atoms of the same element are identical
questions.explanation: This law describes that when elements form more than one compound, the ratios of masses are simple whole numbers.

questions.questionText: Which of the following trends decreases across a period?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge pulling electrons closer.

questions.questionText: Who discovered that the atom has mostly empty space?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed atoms are mostly empty space.

questions.questionText: What is the final result of (10.0 + 5.55) / 2.0 when expressed with the correct significant figures?
questions.explanation:
Step 1 (Addition): 10.0 + 5.55 = 15.55. Limit to one decimal place: 15.6. Step 2 (Division): 15.6 / 2.0 = 7.8.

 Limit to two significant figures (from 2.0) or three (from 15.6). The answer is limited by the multiplication/division rule to the least significant figures (two from 2.0), so 7.8.

questions.questionText: The chemical synthesis of ammonia (NH3) by the Haber-Bosch process is vital for which industry?
questions.explanation: Ammonia is the essential starting material for producing nitrogen-based fertilizers, crucial for increasing crop yield in agriculture.

questions.questionText: According to the Law of Definite Proportions, a chemical compound always contains elements in:
questions.explanation: A chemical compound always contains elements in a fixed mass ratio regardless of the sample size.

questions.questionText: Which branch of chemistry deals about the effect and fate of chemical productions in the surrounding?
questions.explanation: Environmental chemistry studies the behavior and effects of chemicals in air, water, soil, and living systems.

questions.questionText: If ionization energy of Al = 578 kJ/mol and Si = 786 kJ/mol, which is correct?
questions.explanation: Ionization energy increases across a period; Si > Al.

questions.questionText: An example of a derived unit in the SI system is:
questions.explanation: Area is a derived unit, typically expressed in square meters (m squared), which is derived from the base unit of length (meter).

questions.questionText: Which experiment proved the existence of the atomic nucleus?
questions.explanation: Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed that atoms have a dense central nucleus.

questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds has a very high melting point?
questions.explanation: Potassium chloride is an ionic compound, which characteristically has a high melting point.

questions.questionText: Which property did Mendeléev primarily use to group elements into columns?
questions.explanation: He grouped elements with similar chemical properties in the same vertical columns (groups).

questions.questionText: Which major branch of chemistry deals with the study of non-carbon containing compounds, including metals, minerals, and gases?
questions.explanation: Inorganic chemistry is the branch that studies the properties and reactions of inorganic compounds, which are generally substances that do not contain carbon-hydrogen bonds.

questions.questionText: Which statement about the relationship between density and temperature is generally true?
questions.explanation: For most substances, as temperature increases, the volume increases (thermal expansion), while the mass remains constant. Since density equals mass divided by volume, the density decreases.

questions.questionText: Which measuring tool provides the highest number of significant figures for a volume measurement in titration?
questions.explanation: The burette is calibrated to dispense and measure variable volumes with very high precision (typically to two decimal places), making it the most precise tool listed for volume dispensing.

questions.questionText:
Given the following periodic table,

To which one of the following do the elements Li to Ne belong? They are in the same
questions.explanation: Li through Ne occupy the same horizontal row, so they are all in Period 2.

questions.questionText: In the molecule Carbon dioxide (C O two), the atoms are bonded by:
questions.explanation: Carbon forms a double bond with each of the two oxygen atoms.

questions.questionText: Why is the study of chemistry essential for food production and preservation?
options: It helps analyze soil composition and determine fertilizer needs.
It is necessary to synthesize protective packaging materials.
It explains the chemical reactions involved in cooking and spoilage.
questions.explanation: Chemistry is applied at all stages: analyzing soil (agricultural chemistry), manufacturing packaging (polymer chemistry), and understanding processes like cooking, digestion, and fermentation (biochemistry/food chemistry).

questions.questionText: Electronegativity values (period 2): Li = 1.0, Be = 1.5, B = 2.0, C = 2.5. Trend shows:
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases from left to right across a period.

questions.questionText: In the formation of the compound Lithium fluoride (L i F), the Lithium atom:
questions.explanation: Lithium (Group 1, a metal) loses its one valence electron to form a L i one plus cation.

questions.questionText: A student added 25 mL of AgNO₃ solution to a beaker and weighed the mass of the beaker and its content as m1. He/she added 50 m.l of a saturated solution of NaCl into the second beaker and weighed the mass of the beaker and its content as m2 .Finally , he/she mixed the two solutions and weighed the mass of the resulting solution with the two beakers and recorded as m3. If he/she found that m3 = m1+ m2, which one of the following laws is investigated by this trial?
questions.explanation: The experiment demonstrates that the total mass before and after a chemical reaction remains constant, which is the Law of Conservation of Mass.

questions.questionText: Which scientist discovered electrons are part of all atoms?
questions.explanation: Thomson discovered the electron in all atoms.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the most important rule when weighing a chemical using an electronic balance?
options: Place the chemical directly on the balance pan.
Use a piece of weighing paper or a beaker to hold the chemical.
Ensure the chemical is dissolved in water.
questions.explanation: Chemicals should never be placed directly on the balance pan as they can corrode the pan or contaminate the instrument. Weighing paper or a tared container must be used.

questions.questionText: Why did Mendeléev leave gaps in his periodic table?
options: He wanted to add more elements later
He predicted the existence of unknown elements
He made a mistake in ordering
questions.explanation: Mendeléev left gaps for elements that were not yet discovered but whose properties he predicted.

questions.questionText: Which of these has highest first ionization energy: Li, Be, B, C?
questions.explanation: Ionization energy increases across a period; C > B > Be > Li.

questions.questionText: A chemical bond that results from the attractive force between shared electrons and nonmetal nuclei is called a
questions.explanation:
A covalent bond forms when two nonmetal atoms share valence electrons, and the shared electrons are **attracted to the nuclei of both atoms, holding them together. 

Ionic bonds result from electron transfer, hydrogen bonds are intermolecular attractions, and metallic bonds involve a 'sea of electrons' in metals.

questions.questionText: If a chemical reaction is represented as A + B} --> C + Heat, what can be concluded about the reaction?
options: It is endothermic and products have higher energy.
It is exothermic and products have lower energy.
It violates the Law of Conservation of Mass.
questions.explanation: The word 'Heat' on the product side indicates that energy is released, meaning the reaction is exothermic and the products (C) have less stored energy than the reactants (A and B).

questions.questionText: The purpose of a thermometer in the laboratory is to measure:
questions.explanation: A thermometer is an instrument designed to measure temperature, which is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.

questions.questionText: Compare reactivity of Cl and F. More reactive is:
questions.explanation: Fluorine is more reactive due to higher electronegativity and smaller size.

questions.questionText: When solid salt (NaCl) is dissolved in water, the solid is the:
questions.explanation: The solute is the substance that is dissolved in the solvent. Since salt is dissolved in water, the salt is the solute.

questions.questionText: The chemical industry contributes significantly to a nation's economy by:
options: Manufacturing basic materials like acids, bases, and salts.
Producing finished goods like plastics, detergents, and fertilizers.
Creating employment opportunities and generating export revenue.
questions.explanation: The chemical industry serves as a foundational sector, producing both raw materials for other industries and consumer products, thus having a broad economic impact.

questions.questionText: What is the standard unit of volume for liquids in the laboratory, equivalent to one cubic centimeter?
questions.explanation: One milliliter (mL) is exactly equal to one cubic centimeter (cm cubed or cc).

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly defines a chemical property?
options: property that can be observed without changing the substance's chemical identity.
property that depends only on the sample's size.
property that describes a substance's ability to undergo chemical reactions and change into a new substance.
property that relates only to the physical state of matter.
questions.explanation: Chemical properties, such as flammability or reactivity, are observed when a substance undergoes a chemical change, resulting in a new substance.

questions.questionText: A certain element has atomic number of 33 and mass number of 75. What is the position of this element in the modern Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: Z = 33 is arsenic, with configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰4s²4p³. Therefore, it belongs to the p-block.

questions.questionText: Which separation method is based on the differential distribution of components between a stationary phase and a mobile phase?
questions.explanation: Chromatography is a technique used to separate components of a mixture by utilizing their different affinities for a stationary phase and their differing solubilities in a mobile phase.

questions.questionText: If the atomic radius of sodium is 186 pm and that of chlorine is 100 pm, which is larger and why?
options: Sodium, because it has fewer protons
Chlorine, because it has more protons
Sodium, because it has more electrons
Chlorine, because it is a non-metal
questions.explanation: Sodium has a larger atomic radius due to fewer protons and weaker nuclear pull on its electrons.

questions.questionText: Which of these compounds is NOT expected to dissolve well in water?
options: Methane (C H four, a nonpolar molecule)
Ammonia (N H three, a polar molecule)
questions.explanation: Water is polar and will not dissolve the nonpolar Methane molecule.

questions.questionText: The ability of a metal to be drawn into a thin wire is a physical property called:
questions.explanation: Ductility is the property that allows a material, typically a metal, to undergo tensile stress and be stretched or drawn out into a thin wire without fracturing.

questions.questionText: What is the force that holds ions together in an ionic crystal lattice?
questions.explanation: Ionic bonds are held together by the strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

questions.questionText: A substance that is a poor conductor of heat and electricity in all states is most likely a:
questions.explanation: Covalent substances lack mobile charge carriers (ions or delocalized electrons), making them poor conductors.
